BLOCKED, nothing shipped. The only source for this table is Figshare deposit 10.6084/m9.figshare.32090683.v1 (Xiang Che, CC BY 4.0), a single file 'Raw dade.xlsx' with one sheet, 56 bare coded headers ('Participants ID', 'SS item1'..'SS item22', 'USI item1-3', 'USC item1-3', 'RES item1'..'RES item12', 'SW item1'..'SW item15'), no codebook, no value labels and no questionnaire. The Figshare metadata's references list is EMPTY and the companion paper -- 'How Social Support Predicts the Social Well-being of K-12 teachers: The Mediating Role of Regulation Emotional Self-efficacy and the Differential Moderating Effects of Upward Social Identity and Upward Social Comparison' -- is not indexed in Crossref or Europe PMC and could not be located on the open web, so there is no paper, supplement or appendix to transcribe from. The INSTRUMENT is identifiable with confidence (Caprara & Gerbino's Regulatory Emotional Self-Efficacy scale: the deposit's own keyword list says 'Regulatory emotional self-efficacy', and the live table is 12 items on a 1-5 scale, exactly the RESE's published shape), but identifying an instrument is not recovering its wording. Two independent reasons this cannot be shipped: (1) NO VERBATIM 12-ITEM LIST IS OBTAINABLE. The administration was Chinese (Chinese K-12 teachers; tags/tags_auto.csv records lang=chi) and the deposit and its supplements contain zero Chinese text -- the xlsx holds only numeric responses. The English fallback is no better: the RESE items originate in a book chapter (Caprara & Gerbino 2001, Edizioni Erickson) that is not open, and the open literature reproduces only scattered EXAMPLE items ('How well can you express joy when good things happen to you?', 'How well can you keep from getting dejected when you are lonely?' -- PMC7673490, PMC8702160, PMC9393478, PMC10968139), never the full ordered 12. (2) EVEN GIVEN A LIST, THE CODE-TO-ITEM TIE IS NOT ESTABLISHABLE. 'RES item1'..'RES item12' are the spreadsheet's own bare positional headers and carry no content; any mapping would rest on assuming Che's column order equals some canonical order. That assumption is not safe here, because at least two Chinese renditions of the RESE are in circulation with DIFFERENT item->factor structures over the same 12 numbered items -- Wen, Tang & Yu (2009, Psychol Sci 32(3):666-8) and Huang, Liu, Zhang & Liang (2012, Chin J Clin Psychol 20(2):158-61), fitted as separate models B and C (df 42 vs 43) in Xu et al. 2026, BMC Psychol 14:787 (PMC13217869) -- and nothing in the deposit says which was used. Reconstructing 12 item wordings from model knowledge and assigning them by assumed order would be exactly the fabricated match SKILL.md forbids. RETRY TEST: NO -- an unchanged retry now hits the same three determinate facts (deposit publishes no wording, companion paper not indexed anywhere, item codes are bare positions). What would have to change: the companion article appearing with an instrument appendix, or the authors depositing a codebook / the specific Chinese RESE version and item order they administered.

(1) MAPPING IS RECONSTRUCTED, not sourced: the deposited file (Frontiers Data_Sheet_1, figshare 21515877) has bare headers A1..A48 with no variable labels, and the paper reproduces no RSES item wording (only one example, 'I have lots of good qualities'), so A25..A34 = RSES items 1..10 is inferred from questionnaire position. (1984)'s 8 filler positions (1 in 735471 by chance), so the A-numbers are canonical instrument positions in instrument order. Nothing distinguishes A27 from A28. (2) LANGUAGE FALLBACK: administered in Chinese (Ji and Yu, 1999 adaptation); neither the deposit (one CSV, zero CJK characters) nor the paper carries the Chinese wording, so canonical English Rosenberg (1965) wording ships in the base fields with language=Chinese and the _translated columns omitted. (3) option_text SHIPS BLANK. The paper states a 4-point scale '1 = very conformity to 4 = very inconformity', but the deposited values are already keyed toward high self-esteem: 36 of 45 inter-item correlations are positive (up to +0.45) and item-rest r is +0.27..+0.48 for nine items, which a raw 5-positive/5-negative RSES cannot produce. So resp=1 does not mean the same anchor on every item and the published anchors cannot be attached per item without assuming the (unverified) polarity of each position. A34 is the lone exception (item-rest r = -0.16, mean 1.49 vs 2.2-3.2 for the rest), consistent with one item left unreversed when the others were scored; flagged, not resolved.

BLOCKED on the item-text rights rule (irw#1891, references/itemtext_standard.md 'Rights: when item wording may not be shipped'). NO __items.csv written. The instrument is the Thai Short Version of the Revised Experiences in Close Relationships questionnaire (ECR-R-18); the live item codes ecr1..ecr18 and resp 1-7 were confirmed via irw_table_sets (3,240 rows, 180 respondents x 18 items, every item 1-7). The item wording IS fully recoverable -- Wongpakaran & Wongpakaran (2012) Clin Pract Epidemiol Ment Health 8:36-42, PMC3367387, Table 1 prints all 18 items numbered 1-18 with their English wording, and the PLOS S1 SPSS file's own variable labels give a terse Thai keyword tag per ecrN that matches item N one-for-one (ecr1 'ecr ไม่แสดงความรู้สึก' = 'I prefer not to show a partner how I feel deep down'; ecr13 'ไม่ยากที่จะใกล้ชิด' = "It's not difficult for me to get close to my partner"). Two independent stated non-commercial restrictions bar shipping that wording. (1) The instrument author's own distribution page for the ECR-R (labs.psychology.illinois.edu/~rcfraley/measures/ecrr.htm, FAQ 'Do I need permission to use these scales in my research?') states: "The scales were published in a scientific journal for use in the public domain. You do not need to contact any of the authors for permission to use these scales in non-commercial research. You may not use the scales for commercial purposes without permission." This is the TIMSS 2003 pattern ruled on 2026-09-04 -- a public-domain sentence sitting beside an NC clause -- and the standard states the restriction governs. (2) The only publication of the 18-item ECR-R-18 selection and its Thai adaptation, Wongpakaran & Wongpakaran (2012), is licensed CC BY-NC 3.0: "This is an open access article licensed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial License ... which permits unrestricted, non-commercial use, distribution and reproduction in any medium, provided the work is properly cited." RETRY TEST: NO -- an unchanged retry would reach the same verdict. This is determinate (licence/rights-holder terms bar reuse), not an access failure; the sources were all reached and read. It would take either the rights holder relaxing the restriction, or an IRW-level ruling that a 'non-commercial research' permission statement of this form does not fire the irw#1891 rule. SCOPE NOTE for whoever triages: this is not specific to chinvararak_2021_ecr -- it applies to any IRW table whose wording is the ECR / ECR-R / ECR-R-18 / ECR-S, so it is worth ruling once at corpus level rather than per table. || AMENDED 2026-09-04 after the ECR-R ruling: reason (1) above NO LONGER STANDS. The rule is that the licence of the SOURCE IRW copies from governs, not the instrument rights holder's own terms -- Fraley's 'non-commercial research' statement restricts administering the ECR-R and does not narrow what an openly licensed publication published. A table whose ECR wording comes from a CC BY source now SHIPS, carrying wording_rights=NC plus an issues-page entry (see alsuhibani_2022_ecrs_s3). This table stays BLOCKED on reason (2) alone, which is untouched: the only publication of the 18-item Thai selection, Wongpakaran & Wongpakaran (2012), is CC BY-NC, and that is a SOURCE-level restriction. To unblock: a non-NC source printing the ECR-R-18 wording in the order this study used.
